title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
disposition_detail: The complaint was sustained overall. Issues 1 and 2 were answered No: Presbytery adequately investigated and could use BCO 38-1. Issues 3 and 4 were answered Yes: the confession was inadequate and the admonition was not properly completed. Presbytery was directed to amend the confession, sponsor another reconciliation meeting, record its satisfaction, or pursue further discipline if necessary.
first_summary: Ruff challenged Nashville Presbytery’s investigation and its resolution of allegations against a minister through confession and admonition without formal process. The SJC upheld the investigation and use of BCO 38-1, but held that the abstract confession failed to acknowledge particular sins against particular people and that Presbytery had not shown the admonition’s reconciliation requirement was completed. It ordered an amended confession, another reconciliation meeting, and further action if the spiritual requirements remained unsatisfied.
summary: Ruff challenged Nashville Presbytery’s investigation and its resolution of allegations against a minister through confession and admonition without formal process. The SJC sustained the complaint only on the confession and administration of censure: the investigation was adequate and BCO 38-1 was available, but the abstract confession did not acknowledge particular sins against particular people. Presbytery had to amend it, sponsor another reconciliation meeting, document satisfaction with the proceedings, or pursue the matter further, potentially through indictment.

evidence_notes.dispute: The four challenges concern the adequacy of the BCO 31-2 investigation, use of BCO 38-1, adequacy of the confession, and administration of censure; lines 33–41 (printed p. 567).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Issues 1–2 were answered No and issues 3–4 Yes at lines 43–51. The investigation and BCO 38-1 procedure were upheld at lines 57–78; deficiencies and directives appear at lines 82–92 (printed pp. 569–570).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC did not require formal process categorically; it held BCO 38-1 proper where trial facts were undisputed and formal proceedings waived, lines 72–76. Further action depended on whether repentance, forgiveness, and reconciliation requirements were satisfied, lines 88–92.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The source recounts Case 2009-28’s findings and remand at lines 15–19, but the present judgment is not rendered by incorporating that decision by reference.
